facts.value: You are considered a second degree applicant if you have already completed a first undergraduate degree (e.g. Bachelor's or state examination) at a German university and are applying for another undergraduate degree.
In Hesse, apart from the regular semester fee, no additional fees are charged for a second degree.
The enrollment in a Master's program after completing a bachelor's program does not count as a second degree.
Your studies are considered completed as soon as you have successfully passed the required final examination.
For law and teaching, studies are completed upon passing the first state examination; for pharmacy, upon passing the second part of the pharmaceutical examination.
If you have not yet completed your studies, and you have not received your diploma by the application deadline, it is considered an application for a first degree.
For the restricted degree programs of medicine, dentistry, and pharmacy, you apply for a second degree through hochschulstart.de.
Documents must be submitted by mail to the university by June 15 for the winter semester and December 15 for the summer semester.
For all other degree programs, use the Goethe Campus Portal for application.
In case of applying for DoSV degree programs, prior registration at hochschulstart.de is required.
After logging into the Goethe Campus, you can proceed through the online application.
If the program is not restricted in admission and the application is submitted on time, it is usually approved.
For restricted admission programs, a selection process is carried out and places are awarded based on the results of the first degree examination and reasons for the second degree.
Points are awarded for both the first degree examination results and reasons for the second degree, which are added to a so-called measurement figure.
Based on this measurement figure, all applications are sorted on a ranking list.
Based on this ranking list, the available study places are awarded.
